english.title: Permit use of premises to offer to supply of nitrous oxide for wrongful inhalation
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being

(A)_[the occupier]_
(B)_[concerned in the management]_

of premises, namely **(..SPECIFY PREMISES..), knowingly permitted or suffered to take place on the said premises the offering to supply nitrous oxide, a controlled drug of Class C, to another in contravention of Section 4(1) of the Misuse of Drugs Act 1971, knowing or being reckless as to whether, if it had been supplied in accordance with the offer, it would be likely to be wrongfully inhaled by a person
english.legislation: Contrary to section 8(a) of and Schedule 4 to the Misuse of Drugs Act 1971.

english.notes:
(i) This offence is intended to capture those who permit the use of their premises for the supplying, attempting supply, or offering to supply of nitrous oxide for wrongful inhalation.
(ii) 'Wrongful inhalation' means any inhalation by a person which is not for a medical or dental purpose (for example, the recreational inhalation of nitrous oxide for its psychoactive effect) or is not of nitrous oxide which has been released into the atmosphere (for example, directly from a canister or a balloon), regulation 4C(5). Medical purposes are defined as the purposes of preventative medicine, medical diagnosis or the provision of medical care and treatment, see regulation 2(1) of those regulations.

other.penalty:
Either way
Summary: maximum 3 months imprisonment and / or fine not exceeding £2,500.
Indictment: maximum 14 years imprisonment and / or a fine.
